classification: false-green duplicate overwrite in requirements parser
exact_evidence: _parse_requirements() stores entries by normalized name into a dict via out[_norm(m.group(1))] = m.group(2) with no duplicate detection. Independent mutation demonstration using duplicate governed lines 'bcrypt==5.0.0' then 'bcrypt==4.0.1' produced parser output {'bcrypt': '4.0.1'}, hiding the earlier bad line.
customer_impact: A duplicate governed package line can be masked by last-wins overwrite, manufacturing a false green for exactly the package family this gate is meant to protect.
reproduction_or_mutation_strategy: Feed the parser two bcrypt lines with conflicting versions and observe that it returns only the last one instead of failing closed.
required_action: Reject duplicate normalized package names in requirements parsing before any parity assertion.
closure_gate: The authoritative manifest test must fail immediately on duplicate governed lines and normalized-name collisions.

classification: false-green duplicate overwrite in poetry.lock parser
exact_evidence: _parse_lock() returns {_norm(p['name']): p['version'] for p in data.get('package', [])}. Independent mutation demonstration with duplicate bcrypt package entries (5.0.0 then 4.0.1) produced {'bcrypt': '4.0.1'}, silently hiding the earlier conflicting entry.
customer_impact: A duplicate lock package entry can be hidden, so the authoritative gate can go green even when lock content is internally inconsistent for a governed package.
reproduction_or_mutation_strategy: Feed the parser a synthetic lock package list containing duplicate normalized names and observe last-wins overwrite.
required_action: Add explicit duplicate-name detection for poetry.lock package parsing and fail closed on any repeat normalized name.
closure_gate: The manifest gate must reject duplicate normalized lock package names before asserting parity.

classification: evidence overclaim on complete install-path parity
exact_evidence: The source reconciles direct runtime dependencies only. poetry.lock shows openpyxl 3.1.5 depends on et-xmlfile '*' and locks et-xmlfile 2.0.0, but requirements.txt contains no exact et-xmlfile pin. The ledger nevertheless describes the two install paths as resolving identical runtime versions / runtime manifest parity, which is stronger than the committed source can prove for the full transitive pip path.
execution_flow: Runtime dependency truth and evidence review
customer_impact: Reviewers may infer full transitive lock parity of the pip path when the source only guarantees direct-manifest parity; reproducibility remains weaker for transitive resolution.
reproduction_or_mutation_strategy: Compare direct pyproject dependencies to requirements and poetry.lock, then inspect openpyxl -> et-xmlfile in poetry.lock and note the absence of an exact pip-side transitive pin.
required_action: Narrow the claim to direct-manifest parity or pin/govern the required transitive packages if complete pip-vs-lock parity is required.
closure_gate: Evidence text must not claim complete installation-path parity unless the pip manifest is transitive-exact or equivalent governance is added.
